To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we systematically analyzed the detection preferences of seven different phosphotyrosine-specific antibodies for each of three phosphorylated EpiYA motifs in CagA, and found that only 9–12 amino acids containing the EpiYA motifs are required and sufficient for specific detection, but the sequence recognition by different antibodies was found highly variable.
the phosphorylated East-Asian CagA Epiya-motif A and D peptides are recognized by most of the commercially available phosphotyrosine-antibodies, but not the B-motif peptide.

the minimal phospho-peptide sequences for the three EPIYA-moities A, B and C of East Asian CagAs are YEEIPQY, YEEIPEY and YEEVQY, respectively, and the seven different anti-phosphotyrose antibodies tested show high variability in their binding preferences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic analysis of phosphotyrisine antibodies recognizing single phospho-EPIYAmotifs in Caga of East Asian-type H. pylori strains.
the detection of phosphotyrosines on CagA and provides valuable information for the use of anti-phosphotyosines antibodies in the future.
the development of specific phosphotyrosine detection tools for CagA and provides the basis for the future design of specific phospho-epitope antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pan-phosphotyrsine antibodies used in this study are not suitable for the detection of phospho-CAGA EPIYA motifs.
the use of pan-phosphotyosine antibodies is a useful and reliable tool for the detection and characterization of phospho-CagaA in East Asian-type H. pylori strains.
only a limited subset of commercially available pan-phosphotyosine antibodies can be used for the analysis of CagA E. pylori strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

only four out of seven pan-phosphotyrisine antibodies were found to recognize all three phosphorylated East Asian-type CagA EpiYA-motifs similarly well, and that only 9–12 amino acids of each phosphorylated EPIY-motif are sufficient for detection by the antibodies.
only four of the seven anti-phosphotyosine antibodies tested here were suitable for the detection of phosphorylated EPIYAs, and these antibodies should be preferred for future investigations.
the use of a combination of at least two different phosphotyrosine-antibodies would be recommended to avoid any false negative results in future studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of different phosphotyrosine-specific antibodies may lead to different conclusions in the detection of phospho-CaGA.
the use of different phosphotyrosine-antibodies may yield different results, thus it is recommended to test the antibodies for their binding preference for each individual EPIYA-type.

the use of different anti-phosphotyosine antibodies is not recommended for the detection of phospho-EPIYAmotifs in Caga, and that the use of a panel of at least three different phosphotyrosine-specific antibodies is required to ensure reliable results.
